summary: An exec gate that says not yet checks again after 5 s instead of 1 min, still doubling up to every 15 min

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change; gate results keep their shape and check numbers.

schema.detail: No table, index or migration change.

compatibility.detail: Recheck waits after not yet are 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, then 900 s (were 60, 120, 240, 480, then 900 s). An exec gate answers about state the graph does not observe, so nothing else wakes it; a host-deploy admit gate waiting for a remote host to go idle measured 129 s of dead time after the condition held. Starting at 5 s keeps the unseen wait within about the time already waited. A gate that keeps saying not yet runs 4 more checks in its first ~10 minutes (each a supervised exec plus gate.requested, runtime.observed and gate.result claims, the result keeping up to 4 KB of output); after that it checks every 15 min as before, so a long wait costs the same per day. Conditions the graph observes should use field or exists gates, which a change wakes at once.

downtime.detail: No restart or migration beyond a normal deploy.

recovery.detail: A gate already waiting is judged against the new schedule at its next evaluation, which a pass or a change triggers; its armed timer can still fire at the old time.
